summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 (FUSE and WinFsp Rust integration with grant-root awareness) for CipherBox — a large Rust port of the node/v3 model to the desktop FUSE/WinFsp stack, including grant-root scope algorithm, rotation engine, and grant-gated read/write paths, using GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows with worktree-isolated parallel execution.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 was fully planned (18 plans across 7+ waves) and executed through 3 successive architectural re-scopes (adding write-plane emit infra, write-owner materialization, and finally an 11-slice atomic grind rewriting ~10k lines of crates/fuse). The combined 69-18+69-09 unit merged with full workspace cargo-green and unit tests passing, but desktop-e2e validation was found structurally unreachable (root-key recovery stub) so the user redefined the merge gate; remaining work (69-10, 69-13, 69-14/WinFsp) is still pending.

repo: gsd-tools commit helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry.

Executor agents sometimes mis-report `expected_base`/worktree metadata as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork base — verify via `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.
cargo fmt run on a crate root can over-reformat unrelated files due to rustfmt-on-mod-declarations drift; executors must scope-check and revert out-of-scope reformats before committing.
crates/fuse worktrees lack node_modules, so husky pre-commit/lint-staged fails on first commit; either run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` or use `--no-verify` for pure-Rust changes.

Project convention: crypto correctness is validated via SDK unit tests (KAT vectors), while FUSE-level correctness is validated via live E2E (sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e with docker+TEE) — legacy FUSE unit tests tied to a removed model should be deleted rather than blindly ported, to avoid false-green.

Desktop root read/write key recovery into KeyState for node/v3 vaults is an unwired stub (same class of gap as the web v2.0 client, phase 63) — apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs bridges from the legacy root_folder_key as a placeholder.

SC#6 (single gated read-entrypoint) CI gate greps crates/fuse/src for raw resolve_ipns_verified/resolve_published_node calls, allowing only marked-allowlisted sites (replay.rs, recycle-bin, 69-13 reencrypt) via a `// sc6-allow:` comment marker.

D-07 dual-keying: read plane keyed by ipnsName (SealedChildRef), write plane keyed by childId UUID (WriteChildRef); child_id derived consistently via `uuid_from_ino(ino)` on both node sealing and parent ref construction.
Terminal-owner zeroization: parent_read_key/parent_write_key are passed as borrows (&[u8]) and the type system prevents zeroing caller-owned buffers; only self-minted keys get zeroized.
RotationHighWater<S> was not Clone by default; adding #[derive(Clone)] was safe since JsonSidecarFloorStore only holds a PathBuf doing read-modify-write on disk (no state divergence risk).

code.finding: list_folder_owned is the sanctioned SC#6 entrypoint for write-owner tree materialization, recovering per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the same gate as list_folder.

JournalOp does NOT have a parent_metadata: FolderMetadata field as originally assumed by research — that field actually lives in fuse-side MkdirJournalResult (journal_helpers.rs:97), invalidating the first re-scope's 'JournalOp weld' premise.

InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} is a read-WRITE vault-owner state storing ipns_private_key + folder_key/file_key — not a read-only projection like the web 68.2 mirror, which is why a keyless ResolvedChild couldn't drive the FUSE flip.

Desktop root read/write keys are placeholder-bridged from the legacy root_folder_key; real node/v3 root-key recovery into KeyState is not wired, making desktop-e2e structurally unreachable until that lands.

workflow: For very large/risky atomic plans that compile RED mid-flip, chunk the grind into bounded per-session slices on a single shared worktree branch, each committing independently, with a durable committed runbook recording the frozen target shape and carry-forward facts between slices so context/session limits don't lose progress.

When a sub-agent halts with an architectural blocker, independently re-verify its grep/evidence claims against the live tree before accepting or escalating to the user — agents can overstate or (rarely) understate scope.
Canary-execute the first plan of a wave synchronously before fanning out the rest in parallel, to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→build pipeline once cheaply.

When a plan's assumed prerequisite infra doesn't exist, prefer 'expand scope, build the missing additive foundation, re-verify' over forcing the original plan — but recognize this can recurse (happened 3 times here) and put a hard decision point to the user rather than auto-spinning indefinitely.

Maintain a 'workspace-green after every merge' invariant across a long execution chain, and treat any plan that can only reach sdk-green (not workspace-green) as needing to be merged jointly with its dependent consumer plan rather than merged alone.
Session/usage-limit deaths (mid-exploration, zero edits) should be distinguished from genuine architectural blockers — the former just needs a wait-and-retry, not a re-scope.
Durable scratchpad handoff files (outside git) are essential for surviving both scheduled pauses and unplanned context compaction across a multi-hour, multi-agent grind.

friction: gsd-planner and executor agents suffered multiple mid-stream API errors/stalls (connection closed, response stalled, session-limit hit) requiring manual recovery/resumption from partial worktree state.

Three successive architectural discoveries during execution (missing write-plane emit API, missing write-owner materialization, and finally the ~10k-line atomic FUSE rewrite being far larger than scoped) repeatedly invalidated prior planning/research passes.
cargo check --workspace (lib-only) hid ~200 test-compile errors that only surfaced under cargo check --tests, causing an underestimate of remaining Slice 5 work.

The user-chosen merge gate (live sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e) turned out to be structurally unreachable due to an unrelated pre-existing stub (desktop root-key recovery), forcing yet another user decision late in the process.
Assistant mis-typed a scratchpad file path (doubled 'phase69' segment) requiring a follow-up move to correct it.
gsd commit-helper false-negative reporting recurred on nearly every commit throughout the session, requiring constant manual git log verification.
